title: Implement blocked GF(p) invert via PLE (026fc832 Phase 6)
description:
Phase 6 implementation task under epic `026fc832`. Implements blocked GF(p) invert per design `feb15da9`, building on the panelized PLE implementation.

Parent epic: `026fc832`. Predecessors: `feb15da9` (design), panelized PLE implementation (sibling).

## Amendment (2026-05-27, user-approved, session 11)

R0 evidence (`dev/bench_results/2026-05-27-8df0c501-blocked-invert.md`) closed 8 of 11 A8 invert cells PASS (rows 34, 35, 36, 38, 41, 42, 43, 74). The remaining 3 cells are routed per user-approved decision (session 11 AskUserQuestion: "Investigate GF(251)/n=64 borderline first; amend the rest"):

- **Row 39** (GF(251)/n=256/uniform @ 4.08×): `[aspirational]` inheriting the `6823c8a0` GF(251)/n=256 PLE-side gap. The blocked invert's `trsm_lower` + `trsm_upper` calls inherit the PLE bottleneck at this cell. Closure requires the blocked Schur-update kernel or float-cascade PLE work tracked under 6823c8a0's existing [aspirational] amendment.
- **Row 37** (GF(251)/n=64/uniform @ 1.566×): deferred to follow-up task `d36cc414` (GF(251)/n=64 borderline investigation).
- **Row 40** (GF(251)/n=256/deficient @ 1.707×): deferred to follow-up task `d36cc414` (GF(251)/n=64 borderline investigation covers the same dispatch-path overhead pattern at GF(251) sizes near the panel threshold).

## Amendment (2026-05-27, user-approved, session 12 — resolves session-11 deferrals)

`d36cc414` returned branch (b) — structural-gap analysis (evidence at `dev/bench_results/2026-05-27-d36cc414-gf251-n64-borderline.md` § 6). Session-11 deferrals resolved:

- **Row 37** (GF(251)/n=64/uniform): d36cc414 measured 1.524× (paired tight-session). Decomposition shows 74% of wall time in the two TRSM calls (lower + upper) with n_rhs=64, each driven by recursive bisection down to `TRI_BASE_THRESHOLD = 8`. Scalar `trsm_*_base` work at m=8 is the dominant cost. Closing this gap requires the same SIMD `trsm_base` new-kernel work as row 23 (out of scope for `8df0c501`). **Mark `[aspirational]` at 1.524×** (user-approved 2026-05-27).
- **Row 40** (GF(251)/n=256/deficient): d36cc414 measured 1.672× (paired tight-session). Decomposition shows 100% of wall time in the panelized PLE itself (rank-deficient input → invert returns None immediately). Closing this gap requires either a different PLE algorithm for n=256 deficient inputs (e.g., aggressive early-termination as fflas does) or a wider PLE kernel using packed F32 arithmetic. Both are out of scope for `8df0c501`. **Mark `[aspirational]` at 1.672×** (user-approved 2026-05-27).

## Background

Closes A8 rows 34-43, 74 (invert cells over GF(7/251/65521) and GF(31)).

- [hard] Production code implementing the blocked invert per the approved design.
- [hard] Bit-exact correctness: A * A⁻¹ = I for all proptest cases across GF(7), GF(31), GF(127), GF(241), GF(251), GF(65521) at boundary lengths.
- [hard] 5-trial CCX1-pinned benchmarks at n in {64, 256, 1024} per prime.
- [hard] [AMENDED 2026-05-27 — see Amendment blocks above] Every A8 invert cell (rows 34-43, 74) either PASSes (ratio ≤ 1.5× vs fflas) OR carries an explicit user-approved [aspirational] amendment. Row 39 is [aspirational] at 4.08× inheriting 6823c8a0's GF(251)/n=256 PLE-side gap. **Row 37 is [aspirational] at 1.524× per d36cc414 branch (b) evidence (session 12).** **Row 40 is [aspirational] at 1.672× per d36cc414 branch (b) evidence (session 12).**
- [hard] No regression on currently-PASSing cells (delta ≤ 5%).
- [hard] No `unsafe` outside kernel crates.
- [hard] Reuses panelized PLE + `fp_small_try_gemm_classical`.

- [hard] Every A8 invert cell (rows 34-43, 74) either PASSes or carries [aspirational] amendment.
